comments.author: @monikaliebold4225
comments.text:
Everyday life on Mo'orea is probably a little different from what people might picture when thinking of a tropical island. I moved here four years ago, and I've come to know and love not only the beautiful scenery but also the everyday life of the island.
Of course, we are surrounded by stunning beaches, turquoise lagoons and lush green mountains, but life here is much more than a holiday postcard. I think everyday life on tropical islands is sometimes a little romanticised from the outside. We are living in the 21st century, after all! Mo'orea has modern infrastructure, schools, supermarkets, smaller shopping centres, shops, restaurants and medical facilities. Cars are particularly important here, as they are essential for getting around and staying mobile on the island. People use smartphones and the internet just like everywhere else – and yes, Mo'orea even has fibre-optic internet!
People go to work, raise families, do their shopping, take their children to school, attend appointments, meet friends and enjoy their free time. In other words, life here comes with all the same everyday routines and responsibilities as anywhere else.
At the same time, Polynesian culture, traditions, music, dance and traditional craftsmanship are very much alive. They are lovingly preserved and passed on from one generation to the next. This beautiful combination of modern everyday life and a rich cultural heritage is part of what makes living here so special.
At the end of the day, Mo'orea is not just a beautiful holiday destination. It's home to a community of people living perfectly normal, modern everyday lives – just in a pretty extraordinary setting.
And as for me, I'm very happy to call this beautiful island home. Four years ago, I made the decision to move here, and I haven't regretted it for a single moment. I certainly have no plans to move back. I've found my place in the world, and I couldn't imagine a better place to call home.
